llm.summary: This skill does what it claims, but it can send Feishu messages using local app credentials with weak scoping and validation.

dimensions.detail: Access to ~/.openclaw Feishu credential files and journal logs is plausible for the stated workflow, but it is high-impact and under-scoped because it may use unintended readable agent configs and encourages extracting user identifiers from logs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hook, background service, dependency installer, or remote payload retrieval was found; the package contains documentation, metadata, and a local shell script requiring jq and curl.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documentation says the agent should be ass or ops, but send.sh accepts any agent name and derives a credential-file path from it; recipient type, target, and message are also not allowlisted or safely JSON-encoded.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism or privilege escalation was found, but the script uses existing local Feishu credentials to act as a bot identity and does not require an explicit confirmation step before sending.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The Feishu messaging purpose is coherent, and the network calls go to Feishu APIs, but the skill reads local app secrets, obtains tenant tokens, and sends user-supplied message content to external recipients.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the publisher and intend agents to send Feishu messages with local app credentials. Restrict readable ~/.openclaw credential files, allow only intended agent identities and recipient types, avoid sending sensitive content, and prefer adding confirmation, recipient allowlists, and safe JSON construction before routine use.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: Outbound Feishu messaging is the core purpose, but the artifacts do not clearly warn that message content and recipient identifiers leave the local environment or define consent and recipient controls.
[E1] expected: The external transmissions are to official Feishu endpoints and are purpose-aligned, so this is not malicious exfiltration by itself; the concern is the lack of guardrails around what is sent and to whom.
[T05] unexpected: The unvalidated agent argument can select any readable ~/.openclaw/openclaw-<agent>.json file, which is broader than the documented ass/ops scope.
[T09] unexpected: Manual JSON and URL construction with unsanitized target, recipient type, and message values can corrupt or alter outbound requests; this is an implementation weakness rather than evidence of malware.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-only documentation and zh-CN tagging fit a Feishu-focused workflow and do not materially affect the security verdict.
[SDI-4] expected: The msg_type naming mismatch is a documentation clarity issue; it does not add independent malicious behavior.
